STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, shallow, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall shadow).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, around 24-26 cm.
b) Reference: an almond is 2.3 cm. The plate spans roughly 10-11 almond lengths across its diagonal-ish width on the visible side, so width is about 10.5 x 2.3 = 24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square, area 625 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Almonds (countable): I count about 45 visible almonds in a spread, mostly one layer with some stacking in the centre. Add hidden ones under the pile, roughly 5-8 more. Total about 50 almonds x 1.2 g = 60 g.
- Footprint check: the almond cluster covers about 20% of the plate area (about 125 cm2). Thickness is roughly 2 almonds deep at the centre (about 2.5 cm), average about 1.2 cm. Volume = 125 x 1.2 = 150 ml. Almond bulk density is roughly 0.6 g/ml for whole nuts with air gaps, giving 90 g. This is close to the count-based estimate, so I take the count-based value of about 60 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible under the almonds; the plate surface is bare. No extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy: raw almonds are about 575-580 kcal per 100 g. These look roasted/plain, so use 579 kcal/100 g.

Totals: 60 g almonds, about 348 kcal.
